title: CAT 2021 Question Paper (Slot 1, PYQ) - Quantitative Ability - Time, Speed and Distance
subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: Two trains cross each other in 14 seconds when running in opposite directions along parallel tracks. The faster train is 160 m long and crosses a lamp post in 12 seconds. If the speed of the other train is 6 km/hr less than the faster one, its length, in m, is
questions.explain:
Speed of the faster train = $\frac{160 \text{ m}}{12 \text{ s}} = \frac{40}{3}$ m/s.
Convert the speed difference (6 km/hr) to m/s: $6 \times \frac{5}{18} = \frac{5}{3}$ m/s.
Speed of the slower train = $\frac{40}{3} - \frac{5}{3} = \frac{35}{3}$ m/s.
Relative speed when moving in opposite directions = $S_1 + S_2 = \frac{40}{3} + \frac{35}{3} = \frac{75}{3} = 25$ m/s.
The distance covered when crossing each other is the sum of their lengths = $L_1 + L_2 = 160 + L_2$.
Time taken = $\frac{\text{Total Distance}}{\text{Relative Speed}} = \frac{160 + L_2}{25} = 14$ seconds.
$160 + L_2 = 350 \implies L_2 = 190$ m.
